analysis: Integration of the six units; no supported finding. Production change is one call in provider-swift/Sources/darkbloom/SwitchCommand.swift (head lines 36-37): ModelScanner.configureCacheDirectory(snapshot.configuredModelCacheDirectory) after loadRuntimeSnapshot(configPath:) and before the local-model scan. This makes `darkbloom switch` scan the same model_cache_directory as the running daemon (issue #1469). The directory comes from the operator's own provider.toml, whose path is already taken from the daemon state file. The unchanged live-state and process-identity checks, the lifecycle mailbox request, and the daemon-side artifact and hash validation remain. A local actor who can edit provider.toml could already redirect the cache (A-004, T-012, TB-003, T-027), so no new capability is added. The scan only enumerates model IDs. It does not touch encrypted prefix-cache storage (T-041), key custody, App Attest authorization (TB-011, T-053), the WebSocket or the fan helper. The docs line in docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head 296-297) and changelog.d/switch-model-cache-directory.md only describe this behavior. The new test (SwitchCommandTests.swift head 108-126) is test-only. It uses a sandboxed child process, but the CLICommandSandbox and runFailingCLICommand helpers were not supplied, so sandbox isolation from real user state is unverified. Open questions outside the evidence: ModelScanner.configureCacheDirectory and loadRuntimeSnapshot were not supplied, so their path validation (symlinks, relative paths, tilde expansion) and the daemon's re-validation of the selected model's weight hash on a custom directory are unverified. Process-global scanner state in a short-lived CLI poses no visible cross-request risk. I raise no finding and flag no security-relevant uncertainty requiring deeper review beyond these coverage limits.
